task.swarm_objective: Produce a comparative analysis of NVIDIA and AMD's AI-related business performance, supported by financial filings and recent earnings information.
task.agent_directive: Investigate AMD's data-center segment revenue growth (Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs): reported figures, drivers, and cited sources.
constraints: Cite a source for every financial figure you record.
Use the most recently reported fiscal periods.
Focus on the Data Center segment only.
success_criteria: Identify reported Data Center segment revenue for recent quarters
Explain contributions from Instinct and EPYC

tool_arguments.query: AMD Data Center segment revenue Q3 2026 Instinct EPYC

events.content: AMD Data Center segment revenue Q3 2026 Instinct EPYC

AMD has **not yet reported Q3 2026 results** as of October 17, 2026, so no actual Q3 Data Center segment-revenue figure—or disclosed Q3 split between Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs—is available. 

For Q3 2026, AMD’s guidance is for **total company revenue of approximately $13.0 billion, plus or minus $0.3 billion**; it did not provide Data Center segment guidance in that release. [[1]] 

The latest reported segment result is **Q2 2026 Data Center revenue of $6.7 billion**, up **107% year over year**, driven by strong demand for **AMD EPYC processors** and **AMD Instinct GPUs**. [[1]] 

Management said it expected Data Center sales to **accelerate in the second half of 2026**, citing accelerating EPYC demand, scaling Instinct deployments, and the beginning of the Helios ramp. [[1]]

Sources:
[S1.1] AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) — https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1295/amd-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results

source_references.title: AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD)

tool_arguments.query: AMD Q2 2026 Data Center revenue split Instinct EPYC

events.content: AMD Q2 2026 Data Center revenue split Instinct EPYC

AMD did not disclose a dollar revenue split between Instinct accelerators and EPYC server CPUs for Q2 2026; it reported them together within its Data Center segment. [[1]] 

Data Center revenue was **$6.718 billion** in Q2 2026, up **107% year over year**, with AMD attributing the performance to strong demand for both EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs. [[1]] 

The available qualitative detail is that EPYC sales increased by **more than 70% year over year**, while Instinct sales **more than doubled year over year**, but neither figure was quantified in dollars; therefore, an Instinct-versus-EPYC revenue allocation cannot be reliably calculated from AMD’s reported results. [[2]]

Sources:
[S2.1] AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) — https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1295/amd-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results
[S2.2] Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) Q2 FY2026 earnings call transcript — https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/earnings/AMD-Q2-2026-earnings_call-660937.html

tool_arguments.query: AMD Data Center segment definition fiscal 2026 annual report

events.content: AMD Data Center segment definition fiscal 2026 annual report

AMD’s annual report filed February 4, 2026 (for the fiscal year ended December 27, 2025) defines the **Data Center** reportable segment as primarily including “AI accelerators, CPUs for servers, GPUs, APUs, DPUs, AI NICs, FPGAs and SoC products for data centers.” [[1]] 

The filing further characterizes the segment’s product mix as server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, AI NICs, FPGAs, and adaptive SoC products that address computational, visual-data-processing, and AI-workload-acceleration requirements in data centers. [[1]]

Sources:
[S3.1] February 4, 2026 - 10-K: Annual report [Section 13 and 15(d), not S-K Item 405] — https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0000002488-26-000018/amd-20251227.htm
